title: Local models of the fibres of a composite
statement: Let $a:U\to X$ and $f:X\to S$ be locally finite type morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $u\in U$, $x=a(u)$, $s=f(x)$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{U_s,u}$ and $C=\mathcal O_{U_x,u}$, using scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and local rings (structure-sheaf stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]). These are Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; the induced map $A\to B$ is local (the inverse image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ is $\mathfrak m_A$), its closed fibre is canonically $B/\mathfrak m_A B\cong C$, and it is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] if $a$ is flat at $u$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Each of the three pointed fibres admits an affine open neighbourhood of its indicated point that is finite type over its ground field, namely $\kappa(s),\kappa(s),\kappa(x)$ respectively [def-weil-residue-field]. The stalks and residue fields on these neighbourhoods identify with the indicated fibre stalks and with $\kappa(x),\kappa(u),\kappa(u)$ respectively, compatibly with the residue-field tower $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$.
